name: Lidar rover (TurtleBot-style)
summary: A TurtleBot-style differential-drive base for ROS 2: two 37 mm encoder gear motors, two ball casters, a Raspberry Pi 4 running SLAM on a 360 degree RPLIDAR C1, three round plates and a 3S 18650 pack.

spec.name: Lidar Rover
spec.function: A differential-drive robot base in the TurtleBot style: two 12 V encoder gear motors on an L298N drive the wheels, ball casters front and back carry it, a Raspberry Pi 4 runs ROS 2 SLAM and navigation from a 360 degree RPLIDAR C1 on the top plate, and a 3S 18650 pack with a 5 V step-down powers everything.
spec.quote: Let's build our own TurtleBot: round three-deck base, two encoder gear motors and two ball casters, a Raspberry Pi 4 for ROS 2 and an RPLIDAR C1 on top for SLAM, running off three 18650s. It has to carry a 2 kilo payload up a 15 degree ramp, and DC motors shouldn't run near stall, so give each one four times the torque that takes. The top plate can't sag more than 0.3 millimetres or the scan tilts, and with the lidar up high it must not tip before 20 degrees. The pack needs twice the peak current and it should map for two hours. Under 230 euros and 2 kilos.

parts.name: Bottom plate
parts.description: Round plate of 200 mm diameter and 4 mm (Z 19.5 to 23.5) with a clamp saddle 30 x 45 x 22 mm for each gear motor at X=+-56, a cable hole and four standoff holes.

parts.name: Mid plate
parts.description: Round plate of 200 mm diameter and 4 mm at Z 82 to 86 on four 8 mm standoffs from the bottom plate, carrying the Raspberry Pi and the step-down.

parts.name: Top plate
parts.description: Round plate of 200 mm diameter and 4 mm at Z 132 to 136 on four 8 mm standoffs from the mid plate, with a 62 mm seat ring for the lidar.

parts.name: Wheels
parts.description: Two 84 mm wheels, 20 mm wide, on the axle along X at Z=42 and X=+-118, each with a 6 mm hub bore, a groove for an O-ring tyre and five windows.

parts.name: Left drive motor
parts.description: Turns the left wheel, its encoder counts the distance

parts.name: Right drive motor
parts.description: Turns the right wheel, its encoder counts the distance

parts.name: Motor driver
parts.description: Dual H-bridge for both motors, on the bottom plate in front

parts.name: Rear ball caster
parts.description: Carries the back of the base

parts.name: Front ball caster
parts.description: Carries the front, so the base sits on four points like a Kobuki

parts.name: Three 18650 cells, 3S
parts.description: 10.8 V for the motors and the step-down

parts.name: 3 x 18650 holder
parts.description: Holds the cells on the bottom plate behind the motors

parts.name: 5 V step-down
parts.description: Feeds the Pi and the lidar from the pack

parts.name: 360 degree lidar
parts.description: Scans the room for SLAM, on the top plate

requirements.text: Each motor carries half of the rover and a 2 kg payload up a 15 degree ramp with at least 4 times the torque
requirements.quote: give each one four times the torque that takes

requirements.text: Top plate sags under 0.3 mm under the lidar
requirements.quote: The top plate can't sag more than 0.3 millimetres or the scan tilts

requirements.text: Tips only beyond 20 degrees with the lidar on top
requirements.quote: with the lidar up high it must not tip before 20 degrees

requirements.text: The 3S pack covers the motor peaks, the Pi and the lidar with at least 2 times headroom
requirements.quote: The pack needs twice the peak current

requirements.text: Maps at least 2 hours on one charge
requirements.quote: it should map for two hours

left-motor.reason: 131:1 gearing gives 45 kg cm at 83 rpm, about 0.37 m/s on 84 mm wheels, and the 16 CPR encoder feeds the odometry SLAM needs.

right-motor.reason: The same motor on both sides so the two wheels match.

motor-driver.reason: Two channels at 2 A each from 10.8 V; the motors draw about 0.35 A cruising.

rear-caster.reason: Steel ball with spacers sets the caster to the 19.5 mm under the bottom plate.

front-caster.reason: A second caster in front keeps the tall rover from pitching forward when it brakes.

cells.reason: 10.8 V matches the 12 V motors, 10 A continuous covers both at stall, 37 Wh for the runtime.

holder.reason: Three cells flat behind the motors keep the centre of mass low and between the wheels and the caster.

computer.reason: Runs ROS 2 with slam_toolbox and the RPLIDAR driver; 1 GB is enough for a 2D map.

buck.reason: 5.1 V, 2 A continuous covers the Pi 4 and the lidar.

lidar.reason: 12 m range at 10 Hz, 360 degrees, a ROS 2 driver, and at 5 V 230 mA it barely touches the budget.
